refusal_contract.sentence: not stated in the provided papers.
refusal_contract.format: not stated in the provided papers. <one-line reason>
refusal_contract.match_rule: case-insensitive substring match of `sentence` after whitespace normalisation
documentation: A model judge reads each answer and labels it, so no code decides correctness.
An answer is a refusal iff it contains the sentence above, after whitespace normalisation and case folding.
required_facts/forbidden_facts are shown to the judge as what the question turns on; they are not string-matched.
An answer that states the fact but in a different phrasing, word order, plural or number format is correct. A judge that rejects it is wrong, not strict.
refused_correctly requires expect == unanswerable; refused_wrongly means the answer refused an answerable question.

grading_rules.judge: a model reads the question, the answer, the cited passages and the paper text, and writes one line into judgments.jsonl
grading_rules.apply: python scripts/apply_judge.py fills answer_grade in results.csv from judgments.jsonl
grading_rules.correct: not a refusal, the facts the question turns on are all stated, no forbidden fact is present, and at least one citation names a paper, section and page
grading_rules.wrong: not a refusal, and a fact is missing, misattributed to the wrong paper, contradicted, or uncited
grading_rules.refused_correctly: refusal on a question with expect == unanswerable
grading_rules.refused_wrongly: refusal on a question with expect == answerable, including refusing because the daily or per-minute limit was hit
grading_rules.answer_grade_gate: answer_grade stays empty unless status == ok; failed requests are counted in the failure columns, never in the quality denominator
grading_rules.note: required_facts and forbidden_facts below are judge guidance. Several answers were previously marked wrong for '4,096' vs '4096' and 'generation more stable' vs 'more stable generations'; the judge accepts those.

questions.question: How much faster is self-attention than recurrent layers, and when is that true?
questions.notes: Prose. Chunk states self-attention is faster when sequence length n < representation dim d. Table 1 (1706.03762v7-0016, p6) is acceptable table evidence but is not required. Retrieved rank 3 for the plain query.

questions.question: Which optimizer did the Transformer use, and what beta2 value?
questions.notes: Prose. Chunk also gives beta1=0.9 and eps=1e-9; forbidden 0.999 is the Adam default, i.e. a wrong read. Retrieved rank 1.

questions.question: What is Inner Monologue and why does Moshi model text tokens of its own speech?
questions.gold_section_path: 3 Model > 3.4 Generative Audio Modeling > 3.4.4 Inner Monologue
questions.notes: Prose. 0056: text stream acts as scaffolding that lifts linguistic quality. 0057: word-level Whisper timestamps align text to the 12.5Hz audio framerate. Query with the word 'monologue' retrieved 0056 at rank 5 but missed 0057.

questions.question: Why does Moshi delay the semantic and acoustic token streams?
questions.gold_section_path: 3 Model > 3.4 Generative Audio Modeling > 3.4.2 Audio modeling > Acoustic delay.
questions.notes: Prose. A slight delay reduces dependencies between sub-sequences at a time step, so a weaker model can approximate the joint distribution. Retrieved rank 2.

questions.question: Why is a ratio loss needed for the dynamic chunking module?
questions.gold_section_path: 2 H-Net Architecture > 2.2 Dynamic Chunking (DC) > 2.2.3 Ratio Loss
questions.notes: Prose. Without regularisation the model keeps nearly all vectors or compresses excessively; ratio loss guides the target compression. Retrieved rank 1.

questions.question: What BLEU does the big Transformer get on English to German?
questions.notes: TABLE-ONLY. 28.4 sits in Table 2 (EN-DE, Transformer big); 27.3 is the base-model row, 41.8 the EN-FR cell of the same row, 25.8 the base-model BLEU in Table 3 (Q07). The task direction must be stated as 'english-to-german' or 'en-de' (see required_facts_any). Text chunk 1706.03762v7-0022 also states 28.4, but the table is the primary source. Retrieved rank 1.

questions.notes: TABLE-ONLY. Table 3 'base' row: PPL(dev) 4.92, params 65 x10^6. Forbidden 4.33/213 are the 'big' row, one line below - a wrong read shows those. Retrieved rank 1.

questions.notes: TABLE-ONLY. Table 4: Mimi (adv. loss only) MOSNet 3.10, MUSHRA 81.0. Forbidden 2.89/58.8 are the 'non adv. only' Mimi row; 3.12 is the SemantiCodec 3kbps row. Retrieved rank 2.

questions.notes: TABLE-ONLY. Table 4 is the Chinese/code benchmark table (caption in 2507.07955v2-0185): H-Net (M3T1+T15+M4) 64M -> 2.705 final PPL. Forbidden 2.697 is the 66M row two lines below, 2.769 is the Transformer (T9) 29M row. Retrieved rank 1.

questions.question: What are the parameter counts of the three headline models?
questions.gold_section_path: 1706.03762: 6 Results > 6.2 Model Variations | 2410.00037: 3 Model > 3.2 The Helium Text Language Model > 3.2.1 Architecture | 2507.07955: 3 Experiments > 3.2 Alternate Language Datasets > Experimental setup for Chinese and code.
questions.notes: MULTI-PAPER, deliberately kept in natural wording. Transformer big = 213 x10^6 (Table 3), Moshi/Helium = 7B (Table 1 caption, also section 1), H-Net = 64M (Chinese/code table). KNOWN MISS: the natural question says 'parameter counts', the table headers say 'Params.', and BM25 does not stem, so the answer chunks rank outside top-8 for a single global query. This is intended to stay unrewarded by plain retrieval and to be recovered only by per-paper retrieval + union, not by rewording the question. Do not 'fix' this entry by adding 'params' to the question: that fits the benchmark to the retriever and inflates the table axis. Gold for Moshi is the table (2410.00037v1-0037), not the prose intro chunk (…-0030), which no phrasing retrieves.

questions.question: Which of these papers rely on BPE tokenization, and which one avoids a fixed tokenizer?
questions.gold_section_path: 1706.03762: 5 Training > 5.1 Training Data and Batching | 2507.07955: 1 Introduction
questions.notes: MULTI-PAPER. 1706 encodes with BPE (~37000 shared vocab); 2507 critiques fixed-vocabulary tokenization and claims a tokenizer-free model matching a BPE Transformer beyond 1B params. Moshi does not state a BPE pipeline, so it must not be credited. RETRIEVAL MISS: 1706.03762v7-0017 did not appear in top-8 for this phrasing (2507 chunks dominated) - gold answer verified to exist in the chunk, just not retrieved.

questions.notes: UNANSWERABLE (off-topic). Corpus is three ML papers. BM25 still returns 5-8 chunks (top score 11.07, all Moshi); with --rerank --score-floor 0 the result set is empty and n_below_floor=25, which is the desired loud failure.

questions.question: What BLEU score does H-Net report for English-to-German translation?
questions.notes: UNANSWERABLE (plausible-but-absent). H-Net reports BPB/perplexity only - verified: the string 'BLEU' appears in zero 2507 chunks. Forbidden values are the Transformer's BLEU numbers, which is exactly what a hallucinated answer would borrow.

questions.question: What word error rate does the big Transformer achieve on English-to-German?
questions.notes: UNANSWERABLE (adversarial, sits next to a real number). 1706 reports BLEU only; 'WER' appears in zero 1706 chunks. WER does exist in the corpus (Moshi, 2410.00037v1-0101..0103), so a lazy model may answer from the wrong paper. Top BM25 hits are the BLEU tables (0025, 0023) - 28.4 is one token away.
